Note::TexAccessor::strip_fonts¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_fonts() const

Remove Wrapper And Declaration Font Syntax¶

strip_fonts() first unwraps every formatting command supported by strip_fmt(), then removes the declaration switches \rmfamily, \sffamily, \ttfamily, \bfseries, \itshape, and \scshape. It is intended for extracting authored text from source that mixes argument-style formatting (\textbf{...}) with scope-style declarations ({\bfseries ...}).

The distinction matters: a wrapper owns a balanced body, which is retained; a declaration changes the surrounding TeX scope and has no argument for this method to consume. Therefore declaration removal leaves surrounding braces in place. strip_fonts() is not a TeX group simplifier, and it does not infer where a declaration’s visual effect ends. Exact control-word boundaries keep names such as \bfseriesExtra intact, while escaped commands and malformed wrappers are preserved.

The result is a newly allocated, whitespace-normalized Text Note with the same rank, shape, and cell order. Reapplying the method has no further effect. Undefined input remains undefined and every defined non-Text dtype rejects. The work is linear in source bytes and requires no rendered-font engine.

Example 1: Scoped Declarations And Wrappers¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A {\bfseries bold} B {\itshape italic} C)",
    R"(\textbf{wrapped} \ttfamily mono)",
    R"(\\bfseries escaped \bfseriesExtra kept)"});
const auto clean = source.tex().strip_fonts();
std::cout << clean << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A { bold} B { italic} C", "wrapped mono", "\\\\bfseries escaped \\bfseriesExtra kept"]

The braces in the first lane remain because they are source grouping, not part of the declaration token. Use a separate brace-aware transformation only if removing redundant groups is also intended.

Example 2: The Supported Declaration Family¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note(
    R"(\rmfamily roman \sffamily sans \scshape caps)").tex().strip_fonts()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"roman sans caps"

Example 3: Idempotence, Undefined State, And Dtype¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\textbf{bold} \bfseries tail)").tex().strip_fonts();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((once == once.tex().strip_fonts()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_fonts().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_fonts();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip fonts Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
strip fonts Int64: rejected
